$comment: TF-C119 runtime witness for `snprintf` on all three legs, and the FIRST example in the tree able to pin the UCRT `_Options` bit at all. WHAT IT WITNESSES: stdio.json ships `snprintf` split the same way `sprintf` is -- elf/macho import the real libc symbol, pe64 carries `synthesize: "snprintf"` because there is NO pe symbol to import. MEASURED: `objdump -p C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll` (2,484 exports) exports NEITHER `snprintf` NOR `__stdio_common_vsnprintf`; it has `__stdio_common_vsprintf` (ordinal 117) and `__stdio_common_vsnprintf_s` (115), and the `_s` twin is a different function, not a spelling variant. msvcrt.dll (the control) exports `_snprintf`/`_vsnprintf`/`vsnprintf`/`sprintf` but STILL not bare `snprintf` -- so unlike the other five printf-family shims, `snprintf` was never importable on pe under EITHER CRT. The synthesized body therefore reuses `sprintf`'s core, `__stdio_common_vsprintf`, adding NO new import at all (verified: the pe64 import table of a snprintf-using binary lists only the three `__stdio_common_v*` cores that were already there), and differs in exactly two arguments -- `_Options` = STANDARD_SNPRINTF_BEHAVIOR (bit 1) instead of sprintf's legacy bit 0, and `_BufferCount` = the caller's REAL n instead of the `(size_t)-1` unbounded sentinel -- plus the header's `r < 0 ? -1 : r` clamp. WHY THIS EXAMPLE EXISTS RATHER THAN LEANING ON shipped_sprintf_ucrt: that example states its own limit -- with an unbounded `_BufferCount` no truncation is reachable, so `_Options` 0, 1 and 2 yield byte-identical output AND an identical return, making a wrong bit INVISIBLE there. It named the missing piece: "pinning _Options properly needs a bounded-buffer consumer (snprintf), not yet shipped." This is that consumer. THE PINS ARE THE EXACT DIVERGENCE POINTS between the candidate behaviours, every one of which is SILENT (none errors, none fails to link). TWO INDEPENDENT WRONG-ARGUMENT FAILURES ARE COVERED and BOTH RED-ON-DISABLE RUNS WERE MEASURED, not asserted -- flipped in synth_stdio_shim.cpp, rebuilt, run on pe64, then restored and re-run green. (a) `_Options` CLEARED (1<<1 -> 0), i.e. the pre-C99 `_snprintf`: the corpus example goes exit 42 -> exit 50 with EMPTY stdout, failing check 1 because the legacy core returns -1 where C99 requires the would-be length 5; a standalone probe shows the same flip verbatim, `snprintf(buf,4,"%d",12345)` giving `A ret=5` -> `A ret=-1`. ★ HONEST SCOPE, because the obvious second claim did NOT reproduce: legacy `_snprintf` is documented to leave the buffer unterminated too, but on the ucrtbase build measured it still wrote the NUL at buf[3] with the bit clear -- so the RETURN VALUE is this bit's only observed discriminator, and NUL placement is deliberately not claimed as one. (b) `_BufferCount` replaced by the `(size_t)-1` unbounded sentinel: exit 42 -> exit 51, failing check 2 because the core writes the whole "12345\0" past the 4 bytes the caller promised, putting '4' at buf[3]; check 3's sentinel byte at buf[4] covers the same fault from the other side. This is the more dangerous of the two and NOTHING in checks 1/4/5/7 can see it, because it corrupts memory rather than text. Restoring each flip returned the example to exit 42. CHECK 8 is specific to this recipe's SHAPE: every previously shipped stdio shim has at most two named parameters before the `...`, but snprintf has three (buf, n, fmt), so the body must derive `ap` at home-slot index 3 -- an off-by-one there reads the format pointer or the count as the first vararg, and the FP operand additionally requires its xmm value be spilled to its own positional home slot, which no integer check can see. ANTI-FOLD: every operand AND every buffer size is read from a mutable global, and checks 9's operands are DERIVED AT RUNTIME from a previous snprintf's return value -- a value no pass can know without modelling the C runtime -- so the `release` shippedPipeline arm cannot precompute these strings and reduce the example to a no-op. The same source runs on every target listed below, so it is also a cross-target agreement check; MEASURED, pe64 and elf64-x86_64 produce byte-identical results. ★★ THE DARWIN ARM IS PRESENT, AND IT IS PAIRED TO A DESCRIPTOR ROW — the two landed TOGETHER, in ONE edit, exactly as the earlier version of this note required. HISTORY, kept because it is the reason the arm was ever missing: this example first shipped WITHOUT `arm64:macho64-arm64-darwin-exec`, because stdio.json gated `snprintf` to `availableObjectFormats: ["elf"]` while libSystem's export of it was INFERRED (from `_sprintf`/`_printf`/`_fprintf` already being eager-imported by every macho binary that loads and runs on real Apple Silicon, TF-C113) and NOT MEASURED — the operator's Mac was unreachable and no macOS SDK or .tbd stub existed on the build host. Under the eager-import law a wrong guess breaks EVERY macho binary's LOAD, not just the ones calling snprintf, so an arm against an `[elf]`-gated row would have failed loud `S0001 ... got snprintf` and redded the suite: half of the pair is always red. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-05 on the operator's real Mac over ssh (macOS 26.5.2, arm64) — the measurement that unblocked both halves: with SDK=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk, `grep -rwq -e _snprintf $SDK/usr/lib/libSystem.B.tbd` reports the symbol PRESENT in libSystem's export stub, as are `_vsnprintf _popen _pclose _fileno _sysctl _sysctlbyname _exit _fstat64` in the same pass. ★★ ⚠ THE CLOSING RECIPE THIS NOTE USED TO PIN IS BROKEN AND MUST NOT BE RE-RUN: `nm -gU /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib | grep ' _snprintf$'`. ✔MEASURED on that same host, `ls: /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib: No such file or directory` — modern macOS keeps libSystem in the dyld shared cache and ships no such file — so `nm` on that path returns NOTHING for EVERY symbol and the recipe would have reported a FALSE ABSENT for all nine names above. That is the DANGEROUS direction of wrong under the eager-import law: it breaks no build, it silently withholds a real export and makes the staging look permanently justified. The correct FILE-BASED instrument is the SDK `.tbd` text stub named above, grepped `-w` for the mangled name (so `_snprintf` does not match `_vsnprintf`). ★★ AND THE x86_64 DARWIN ARM IS PRESENT TOO — added by the TF-C121 audit-fix, replacing a paragraph here that the SAME commit had already falsified. THAT PARAGRAPH READ: 'SCOPE OF THIS ARM, stated so a green run is not over-read: it exercises Darwin arm64 only. There is deliberately no `x86_64:macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec` arm and this change adds none — that format declares no `dataImportBinding` (a documented, test-pinned omission in `macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec.format.json`), so ANY `<stdio.h>` TU walls there at `error[K_FormatLacksImportSupport] ... extern DATA import ___stdinp`. MEASURED both BEFORE and AFTER this change.' ⛔ BOTH HALVES WERE WRONG AT THE TIP IT SHIPPED AGAINST. (a) The wall was REMOVED IN THE SAME DIFF: `macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec.format.json` now declares `"dataImportBinding": "got-indirect"`, added as rung (2) of that file's own MEASURED capability ladder — whose closing note even records that a `<stdio.h>`+`snprintf` TU is rc=0 there. An 'AFTER' measurement cannot have been taken. (b) 'test-pinned' was never true: that format's earlier comment said in terms that no test pinned these keys. ✔RE-MEASURED 2026-08-05 at the working-tree tip, THIS example through the real CLI: `--target x86_64:macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec` compiles AND links rc=0, no `error[` line, a 23,805-byte Mach-O whose only printf-family import is `_snprintf (from libSystem)`; and ✔RUN on the operator's real Mac (macOS 26.5.2) through the `darwin/arm64 -> arch -x86_64` Rosetta launcher declared in real-examples/c/sqlite/legs.json, stdout `mix=20|a` / `would=10 back=2` byte-exact, exit 42 — identical to the arm64 arm run in the same session, and for BOTH the baseline AND the `release` arm. ⚠ The release half is stated separately because the runner compiles a release arm ONLY when its baseline arm RAN: on a Windows gate the two darwin release arms are never built at all (the arm-ledger says so in terms — 'compile not attempted: baseline arm did not run'), so a release-only fault on either is structurally invisible to this repo's default gate and can only be measured on the Mac, as it was here. ★ WHY THIS MATTERED BEYOND PROSE: that false claim was the stated reason for withholding the tree's ONLY runtime witness for `snprintf` on the very target this cycle both opened AND fixed a data-corrupting `dataImportBinding` misbind on. A witness omitted for a reason that is not true is a coverage hole with an alibi. exit = 42.
